text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 4.3% today as oil prices dropped on easing Middle East tensions. News of renewed U.S.-Iran peace efforts reduced fears of supply disruptions, sending crude down from recent highs—U.S. oil is now trading at $103.37 a barrel versus the $123 global price. For a refiner like Marathon, lower oil prices compress the profit spread between buying crude and selling refined products like gasoline and diesel.

The stock has already fallen 11.5% over two weeks as geopolitical risk premiums that had lifted oil prices earlier in October have unwound. Refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with ample fuel inventories in storage, meaning there's no supply tightness to support prices—the market is simply repricing oil down as the immediate conflict threat recedes.
